title: Build the Repo That Gets an LLM Engineer Hired

sections.title: Hand-Label a 30-Case Golden Dataset
sections.prompt: Pick one real task from your own work (a support ticket router, a doc classifier, a Q&A bot) and hand-label 30 cases yourself. Then have a second person label the same 30 independently. List every case where your labels disagree, write down why in one sentence each, and resolve it to a final answer. Count your agreement rate before resolution — that number is your baseline for 'vibes-good' versus 'actually-good.'

sections.title: Run Your Own Chunking Ablation
sections.prompt: Take one document you'd retrieve from (a policy doc, a README, a spec) and split it two ways: fixed 512-token chunks, and structure-aware chunks that keep tables, numbered lists, and sections intact. Write 10 questions whose answers span a table or multi-step instruction. Run retrieval against both chunk sets and record the hit-rate for each — the percentage of questions where the correct chunk actually got retrieved.

sections.title: Diagram One Agent's Failure Modes
sections.prompt: Sketch a diagram (boxes and arrows, on paper or in a tool) of one agent workflow you've built or want to build. Annotate three things directly on the diagram: where it retries, where it falls back to a cheaper model, and your target p95 latency plus per-run token cost. If you don't have real numbers yet, write down your target ceiling for each and what you'd measure to check it.

sections.title: Try Context Before Fine-Tuning
sections.prompt: Pick a classification or routing problem you'd normally reach for fine-tuning to solve. Before touching a training loop, put the taxonomy and 5-6 labeled examples directly into a prompt's context window and test it against 20 held-out cases. Record the accuracy and the time spent. Only then decide whether fine-tuning would have been worth the extra weeks — write one sentence on what you'd have needed to see to justify it.

sections.title: Ship the route_ticket.py Pattern on Your Own Data
sections.prompt: Adapt the route_ticket.py structure from the post to a task from your own job: write a function that calls an LLM to classify and explain, build a gold.jsonl of 50 examples you labeled by hand, and write an evaluate() function that prints your own match rate against those labels. Push it as a public repo with a README someone else could clone and run in one command — no notebook-only version counts.

cta: Run the chunking ablation or the route_ticket.py exercise and reply with your actual hit-rate or match-rate number — I want to see the real percentage, not just that you tried it.
